title: Your Teen Doesn’t Need a Confidence Speech Before a Presentation—They Need Reps
summary: Use three short preparation reps—one run-through, one likely question, and one reset line—without taking over your teen’s event.
release_move: The parent offers one bounded practice role; the teen chooses the material, the amount of rehearsal, and how to participate in the event.

core_belief_shift.from: My teen needs a big confidence talk or a parent-designed performance plan.
core_belief_shift.to: I can offer a short practice option, preserve their ownership, and leave the outcome alone.

book_relevance.reason: The War Playbook, Chapter 16, teaches preparation under pressure; this parent guide stays complete without the book.

hero.alt: A teenager practises a presentation at home while a parent listens as a quiet audience member.

social_image.alt: A teenager practises a presentation at home while a parent listens as a quiet audience member.

seo_description: A parent guide for helping a teen prepare for a presentation with one run-through, one likely question, and one reset line, without taking over the event.
